proposals.before: He picked eight thousand of the best troops and marched against the Qin army.
proposals.after: He selected eighty thousand of the best troops and marched against the Qin army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 八萬人 means eighty thousand, not eight thousand.

proposals.before: He selected eight thousand elite troops and advanced to attack the Qin army.
proposals.after: He selected eighty thousand elite troops and advanced to attack the Qin army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 八萬人 means eighty thousand, not eight thousand.

decisions.reason: Chinese 八萬人 is eighty thousand troops; idiomatic “eight thousand” understates the figure by a factor of ten, and “eighty thousand” restores the correct numeral without distorting the sentence.
The same 八萬人 appears in the literal English as “eight thousand”; correcting to “eighty thousand” matches the Chinese numeral while leaving the rest of the calque intact.
